en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Cittāgāra-vagga 50.
The Training Rule on Teaching Secular Sciences.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were teaching worldly lore.
People criticized, grumbled, and complained, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs teach worldly lore? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six teach worldly lore?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are teaching worldly lore?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, could the group-of-six bhikkhunīs teach worldly lore?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...

And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should teach worldly lore, there is an offense of expiation."* (*The full rule includes the context of what constitutes "worldly lore.")
“Whatever nun should teach worldly lore, it is an offense entailing expiation.
Regarding “whatever nun”:
whichever such [nun], and so forth.
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Futile science" (tiracchānavijjā) means:
"Whatever external [text] is unbeneficial. "Should cause to recite":
if he causes them to recite by the word, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for every single word.
If one causes [someone] to recite syllable by syllable, there is an offense of expiation for each syllable.
There is no offense if one causes [someone] to recite a written text.
He causes her to recite for the purpose of memorization; he causes her to recite a protective chant for the sake of guarding herself;
[he does so] for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first-offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The fifth chapter, the Chapter on Picture Galleries, is finished.
